where: Section 2, features paragraph on hands-free use
problem: 'Hands-free use matters when the user is holding a tool or a patient' reads oddly: a user holds a tool, but does not hold a patient; a surgeon's hands are on or near a patient.
fix: Write: 'Hands-free use matters when the user's hands are busy: a technician holding a tool, or a surgeon whose hands are on a patient.'

problem: The example says a tablet shows the overlay while the camera stands on a desk, 'so students pass it around'. If the camera is fixed on the desk, moving the tablet does not change the camera pose, so passing it around does not give new viewpoints. The wording can mislead a student about what the untethered display buys.
fix: Write: 'Wireless displays help education: the camera sits on a desk and the untethered tablet shows the registered overlay, so the teacher can carry the display to each student without moving the camera.'

problem: 'Taxonomy of AR' normally means the classification of AR display types (see-through, monitor, projection), not the three tests that define AR. A student may conflate the two.
fix: Write: 'Some syllabi call these three conditions the defining properties of AR; the classification of AR displays into optical see-through, video see-through and so on is a separate topic (Section 2).'
